# PermaDel

> PermaDel is a free, open-source (MIT) secure file shredder for Windows 10 and 11. It overwrites files, folders and their NTFS alternate data streams with 1 to 35 passes of cryptographically secure random data, flushes every pass to disk, then truncates, renames and deletes them, so undelete and file-recovery tools can't bring them back. It's a native WinUI 3 app by Luka Stojiljković.

Key facts:

- Requires Windows 10 version 1809 or later, x64. The "Shred with PermaDel" File Explorer context menu requires Windows 11.
- Optional Windows Hello or account password verification before shredding.
- Refuses drive roots, system folders, user folders and its own folder, even through junctions, mapped drives or short names. Removes links and junctions without touching their targets; skips hard-linked and online-only cloud files.
- Collects no data. Its only network request is a daily update check against GitHub, which can be turned off.
- Verified by 33 unit tests and a forensic test that scans a raw NTFS disk image after shredding.
- Limits: no file-level shredder can guarantee destruction on SSDs or flash media, or of copies in shadow copies, backups or cloud sync.

- [Latest release](https://github.com/lukastojiljkovic/PermaDel/releases/latest): Windows installer, with its SHA-256 hash in the release notes
